content.title: About
content.content: Papaya is a tropical fruit native to Southeast Asia, Central and South America. A ripe papaya has orange‑red flesh, a sweet aroma, and a soft, juicy texture. It is eaten fresh and used in salads, smoothies, desserts, and sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Papaya belongs to the Caricaceae family and is a relative of mango and avocado.
Papaya seeds are edible but have a bitter taste and contain papain – an enzyme that aids digestion.
Warm, humid climates allow the fruit to mature in 6‑9 months.
Papaya is often used in cosmetics for its brightening and exfoliating properties.
In some cultures papaya symbolizes hospitality and abundance.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: One serving provides over 200 % of the daily vitamin C requirement, supporting immunity and protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains papain
items.content: Papain is a proteolytic enzyme that helps improve protein digestion and eases gastrointestinal discomfort.

items.title: Source of vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: Beta‑carotene in papaya converts to vitamin A, essential for vision and skin health.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Potassium, magnesium, and dietary fiber in papaya help regulate blood pressure and cholesterol levels.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavonoids and lycopene in papaya protect cells from free‑radical damage.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to papaya or its seeds, resulting in skin rashes or swelling.

items.title: Lactoferrin content
items.content: High amounts of lactoferrin can cause gastrointestinal upset in sensitive people.

items.title: Pregnancy caution
items.content: Excessive consumption of unripe papaya is thought to stimulate uterine contractions and should be avoided during pregnancy.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut the flesh, discard the seeds, and eat the fruit fresh. It can be added to fruit salads, smoothies, yogurts, or used in sauces for fish and seafood. Dried seeds are sometimes used as a spice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ripe papaya in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer for 3‑5 days. Unripe fruits should be kept at room temperature until they mature, then moved to the fridge.
